title: Will Gold Maintain Its Close Correlation to Inflation?
summary: This article discusses gold's role as an inflation hedge, noting that while short-term correlations may diverge, gold and inflation tend to rise together in the long run. It highlights the Federal Reserve's monitoring of inflation for interest rate decisions and mentions several mining-based funds and stocks (VanEck Vectors Junior Gold Miners Fund, Sprott Gold Miners, B2Gold, Yamana Gold, First Majestic Silver, Hecla Mining) that could be impacted by inflation trends. The article also references specific inflation measures like CPI and PCE.

title: A Booming Global Economy Bolsters Commodity ETFs
summary: The global economy's ongoing growth and improved manufacturing activity are driving increased demand for raw materials, benefiting commodity markets and related ETFs. Major broad commodity ETFs like PowerShares DB Commodity Index Tracking Fund (DBC) and iShares S&P GSCI Commodity-Indexed Trust (GSG) have seen significant gains. Experts predict continued global economic expansion in 2018, which is expected to further boost commodity demand and potentially lead to inflationary pressures.

title: Leadership and Membership Announcements for the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco’s Salt Lake City Branch Board of Directors - San Francisco Fed
summary: Patricia R. Richards has been reappointed as director and chair of the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco’s Salt Lake City branch board for 2018. Additionally, Russell A. (Chip) Childs, president and CEO of SkyWest Inc., was appointed to the board, and Park Price, chairman and CEO Emeritus of the Bank of Idaho, was reappointed as director. These appointments and reappointments are effective January 1, 2018.
source: Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco

title: JPMorgan’s Profits Are Strong, and They’ll Likely Get Stronger (Published 2018)
summary: JPMorgan Chase reported stronger-than-expected Q4 earnings in 2018, despite a $2.4 billion charge related to the new tax law. The bank's results, viewed as a bellwether for the financial industry, indicate that the new lower corporate tax rate will significantly boost future profitability for JPMorgan and its peers, such as Wells Fargo. While its investment bank struggled, JPMorgan's consumer-banking business showed strong growth and is expected to accelerate further with rising interest rates and a strong economy.

title: What UK Manufacturing Activity Indicates for the Economy
summary: UK manufacturing activity in December 2017 saw a decline in its PMI to 56.3, missing expectations, primarily due to slower production, new orders, and employment growth. Despite this, the broader UK economy had shown strong improvement in the preceding months, with GDP growth and rising inflation leading to an interest rate hike. The article notes that while domestic demand weakened, client orders from Europe, China, and the Middle East rose strongly, and the iShares MSCI United Kingdom ETF (EWU) rose by 2.2% in December 2017.

title: Citigroup reports $18 billion loss on one-time tax items
summary: Citigroup reported an $18 billion quarterly loss due to one-time charges related to a new U.S. tax law, despite adjusted earnings beating Wall Street expectations. While the bank faced significant hits from the tax changes, management anticipates long-term benefits, including a lower tax rate and the potential to lift financial performance targets. The bank's shares rose, and consumer banking growth helped offset weaknesses in institutional business.

title: El-Erian: ETFs Could Pop The Bubble
summary: Mohamed El-Erian, Allianz’s chief economic advisor, discussed the potential for a market bubble, emphasizing that while 2017 brought extraordinary market performance, a convergence between fundamentals and valuations is inevitable. He suggested that ETF-driven liquidity mismatches could be one of three major risks, alongside geopolitics and central bank policy normalization, that might lead to increased market volatility in 2018. Despite these risks, El-Erian expressed cautious optimism for economic growth validating asset prices but warned an eventual "bumpier ride."

title: Why Fossil Group, Inc. Stock Dropped Today
summary: Fossil Group Inc. shares fell 13.3% after the company secured less favorable terms for refinancing its $425 million term loan, with annual interest rates significantly increasing. This news led Wells Fargo analyst Ike Boruchow to reiterate an "underperform" rating and increase his estimated per-share loss for Fossil in 2018. Investors are awaiting Fossil's fourth-quarter 2017 results and 2018 guidance in mid-February for more clarity on its financial outlook.

title: Federal Reserve Shackles Wells Fargo After Fraud Scandal (Published 2018)
summary: The Federal Reserve imposed severe penalties on Wells Fargo after years of misconduct, including opening dummy accounts and forcing unnecessary auto insurance. The central bank restricted the bank's growth to its 2017 asset size until it overhauls its risk management and strengthens board oversight. This unusual intervention occurred on Janet L. Yellen's last day as Fed chair, despite a broader effort by Trump-appointed regulators to relax banking rules.

title: A Hedged Bet on a European Bull Market
summary: This article recommends investing in the WisdomTree Europe Hedged Equity Fund (HEDJ) as a hedged bet on European stock markets. The author cites several reasons for this recommendation, including cheaper European stocks compared to U.S. rivals, higher expected corporate earnings growth in Europe, the European Central Bank's quantitative easing program, and the weakening euro boosting export-oriented companies. The fund also hedges against currency risk while focusing on companies with significant revenue generated outside Europe.

title: Betting on the Bull in Japan
summary: This article recommends investing in the WisdomTree Japan Hedged Equity Fund (DXJ) to profit from the Japanese stock market's breakout, citing the Bank of Japan's expanded quantitative easing, a short covering rally, and increased pension fund allocations to equities. It also provides updates on other portfolio holdings like Visa, Vipshop Holdings, and Gilead Sciences, recommending to raise stop-loss orders for some positions. The author emphasizes that DXJ is designed to benefit from both Japanese market gains and a weakening yen.

title: Global Stocks Rebound Strongly
summary: Global stock markets experienced a strong rebound, with the Dow Jones, S&P 500, and NASDAQ all showing significant gains. The MSCI Emerging Markets Index performed particularly well, and several "Alpha Investor Letter" portfolio holdings, including Cambria Global Value ETF (GVAL) and Skyworks Solutions Inc. (SWKS), saw substantial increases and moved back to "BUY" recommendations. The article also provides updates on specific stock recommendations and adjusted stop-loss levels for various holdings.

title: Looking To Hoard Cash? Consider 4-Week Treasurys
summary: This article suggests 4-week Treasury bills as an attractive option for hoarding cash due to their safety, top-of-the-market yields, and quick reaction to rising interest rates from the Federal Reserve. They offer no credit or interest rate risk and can be purchased commission-free through TreasuryDirect with automatic reinvestment. The author highlights their convenience and how they outperform traditional bank savings options in a rising rate environment.

title: Why Commodities ETFs Can Deliver More Upside
summary: The article discusses how a weak U.S. dollar and increasing inflation expectations can drive commodities ETFs higher. It highlights the PowerShares DB Commodity Index Tracking Fund (DBC) and its correlation with inflation, portraying commodities as a strong diversifier for traditional stock and bond portfolios.

title: Israeli Prime Minister Says Government Should Avoid Moves to Shore Up Dollar
summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu met with tech leaders and stated his belief that government intervention in the foreign exchange market would not help shore up the dollar’s value against the shekel. This comes after Israeli tech companies, whose income heavily relies on exports, expressed concern about the shekel's appreciation impacting their profits. Netanyahu emphasized that past attempts to control exchange rates have failed and that Israel is too small a country to implement such measures effectively.

title: Traders Take Another Look at a Regional Bank ETF
summary: Options traders are showing increased interest in the SPDR S&P Regional Banking ETF (KRE) as the fund has seen a nearly 3% gain to start 2018. This bullish sentiment is tied to expectations of rising interest rates, which are historically beneficial for regional banks by improving net interest margins. One options trader, in particular, made a significant bullish bet on KRE, evidenced by a large call option purchase.

title: Snow has his own definition for Trump
summary: Former U.S. Treasury Secretary John Snow describes President Donald Trump as a "pro-business populist" and discusses the "Goldilocks" period of the global economy, warning of potential complacency. Snow also commented on the turbulent times at CSX Corp. and the impact of Trump's tax cuts and the Federal Reserve's quantitative tightening.

title: Income Acceleration With This Dividend ETF
summary: The VictoryShares Dividend Accelerator ETF (VSDA) focuses on U.S. large-cap stocks with a history of increasing dividends and the highest probability of future dividend growth. Debuting in April 2017, VSDA aims to provide exposure to dividend growth rather than high yield, offering diversification benefits, especially in a rising rate environment. This strategy targets companies that raise dividends cautiously, indicating higher quality and sound balance sheets.

title: Coca-Cola Femsa salva un año difícil y crece a doble dígito
summary: Coca-Cola Femsa reported a 14.7% increase in revenues and 9.4% growth in operating utility for 2017 despite facing challenges such as inflation, input volatility, and a loss from its Venezuelan operations. The company's growth was driven by acquisitions in Brazil and the Philippines, price increases, and volume growth in Central America, even as it recorded a significant loss in Q4 2017 due to a change in accounting methodology for Venezuela. Mexican volumes of Coca-Cola brand specifically decreased by 2.5% due to natural disasters.

title: Deutsche Bank to pay $240 million to end Libor rigging lawsuit in U.S.
summary: Deutsche Bank AG has agreed to pay $240 million to settle a private U.S. antitrust lawsuit accusing it of conspiring with other banks to manipulate the Libor benchmark interest rate. This settlement marks the third bank to resolve such claims by "over-the-counter" investors, following similar agreements by Citigroup and Barclays. The bank denied wrongdoing but settled to avoid litigation risks, with the agreement requiring a judge's approval.

title: HomeStreet's new home in downtown Spokane
summary: HomeStreet Bank has opened its first retail branch in Spokane, consolidating commercial and retail services in a 3,400-square-foot space in the Lincoln Building. This move marks an expansion of the bank's presence in the city, following the launch of commercial lending services two years prior. The new branch aims to offer a unified approach to banking, serving both business and consumer clients, while the bank also plans to introduce the Zelle mobile banking application.

title: Four Directors Will Leave Wells Fargo’s Board (Published 2018)
summary: Wells Fargo announced that four board members will step down in April, fulfilling a prior pledge made after the Federal Reserve penalized the bank for misconduct. While Wells Fargo attributes these departures to "regular succession planning," the company has been under significant pressure from regulators and shareholders to overhaul its board. This move will reduce the board's size from 16 to 12 directors, with the company likely to add new members to diversify skills.

title: Vanguard Short-Term Inflation-Protected Securities Index Fund ETF Shares (VTIP) Interactive Stock Chart
summary: This page provides an interactive stock chart and financial information for the Vanguard Short-Term Inflation-Protected Securities Index Fund ETF Shares (VTIP). title: Intermediate Trade: Home Construction ETF
summary: This article suggests a bullish options trade on the iShares U.S. Home Construction ETF (ITB), a sector expected to benefit from the upcoming home-buying season. The author argues that despite rising interest rates, historical trends and strong demand outweigh concerns, making the sector attractive. A specific vertical call spread strategy is outlined for the ITB ETF.

title: JPMorgan Co-President Sees Possible 40% Correction in Equity Markets
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. co-president Daniel Pinto warned of a potential 20 to 40 percent correction in equity markets within the next two to three years. This projection comes amidst investor concerns regarding rising interest rates and inflation, driven by central bank policies. Pinto emphasized that the severity of the correction would depend on current market valuation levels.

title: BlackRock fund manager sees this as the market’s ‘sweet spot’
summary: A BlackRock fund manager identifies emerging-market debt as the current "sweet spot" for investors, offering a refuge from political noise and concerns over rising U.S. interest rates. Despite daily U.S. political drama and the impending end of easy-money policies, BlackRock believes these bonds provide an optimal investment opportunity. The firm manages $6 trillion in investor money and highlights this strategy as a way to tune out market distractions.

title: Charles Schwab: We are the Walmart of investing
summary: Charles Schwab, founder and chairman of Charles Schwab Corp., likens his company to Walmart, emphasizing their commitment to low costs and high value for investors. The brokerage aims to stay competitive by investing in infrastructure and technology to offer clients the best possible experience. Schwab also stressed the importance of long-term investing amidst market volatility and the need for early financial literacy.

title: Schwab Intermediate-Term U.S. Treasury ETF (SCHR) Stock Price, News, Quote & History
summary: This article provides detailed financial information for the Schwab Intermediate-Term U.S. Treasury ETF (SCHR), including its stock price, historical data, performance metrics, and an overview of its investment strategy. It highlights key financial figures such as net assets, yield, expense ratio, and compares its performance against its category. The fund primarily invests in U.S. Treasury securities with maturities between three and ten years.

title: Why Investors Shouldn’t Panic About 3 Percent Treasury Bonds
summary: This article discusses investor fears surrounding the 10-year Treasury yield crossing the 3 percent mark, a level not seen since 2014. It explains that while rising rates reflect a strengthening economy and can impact mortgages and loan costs, experts like Jerry Paul and Jonathan Golub believe a 3 percent or even 3.5 percent yield is not a catastrophic tipping point for financial markets. Instead, they suggest that any significant market sell-off due to such rate increases would likely be a misunderstanding and an excellent buying opportunity.

title: Eduardo Escasany: "En la medida que baje la inflación, la gente ahorrará más en pesos"
summary: Eduardo Escasany, president of Grupo Financiero Galicia, predicts that as inflation decreases, Argentinians will save more in pesos, fueling a boom in credit. He highlights the solidity of the financial system and the potential for significant growth in mortgage loans, while also raising concerns about government financing in the local market potentially crowding out private sector credit. Escasany emphasizes the importance of tackling the informal economy and the slow but necessary process of building trust in the local currency.

title: La acción de Televisa cierra en peor nivel desde junio 2012
summary: Las acciones de Televisa cayeron a su nivel más bajo desde junio de 2012, cerrando en 54.05 pesos, tras una demanda colectiva en Estados Unidos. Mientras tanto, la Bolsa Mexicana de Valores avanzó 0.95%, impulsada por las ganancias de Alfa y su subsidiaria Alpek, que anunció la compra de una planta en EE.UU. Wall Street, por su parte, experimentó descensos tras el anuncio de la Reserva Federal de un aumento en la tasa de interés.

title: This Sustainable, Trump-Tariff-Hiked Budweiser’s for You
summary: Anheuser-Busch InBev is shifting its Budweiser brand to 100% renewable energy and will mark cans accordingly, aiming to boost sales in the U.S. Amid this sustainability effort, the company faces potential price increases for consumers due to President Trump’s 10% tariff on aluminum imports. CEO Carlos Brito anticipates a 2-3% price hike on Budweiser, which relies heavily on aluminum packaging, while also announcing global renewable energy goals by 2025.

title: HSBC Holdings PLC eyes robust growth in retail banking and wealth management in Taiwan
summary: HSBC Holdings PLC anticipates strong growth in its retail banking and wealth management (RBWM) offerings in Taiwan for the current year, marking Taiwan as one of its eight priority RBWM markets in the Asia Pacific. The company plans service enhancements through digital transformation investments and is focusing on digital initiatives to meet customer needs, following record pretax profits of US$43 million from its Taiwan RBWM businesses last year. These initiatives include launching Google Pay, with Samsung Pay and Apple Pay expected soon, and streamlining credit card approvals and insurance sales processes.

title: James H. Herbert II Appointed to the Federal Advisory Council
summary: The Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco's board of directors has appointed James H. Herbert II, Chairman and CEO (Founder) of First Republic Bank, to the Federal Advisory Council for a one-year term beginning April 1, 2018. He succeeds Robert G. Sarver. The Federal Advisory Council, comprised of one member from each of the 12 Reserve Bank Districts, meets quarterly with the Board of Governors to discuss economic and banking matters.
source: Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco

title: Buy Stocks On Big Sell-Offs, Says Citigroup
summary: Citigroup strategists are advising investors to buy stocks during expected steep sell-offs throughout the coming months, anticipating an 8% rise in global equity markets by year-end. This strategy counters many investors' recent wariness, with Citigroup projecting continued economic expansion and the impact of U.S. tax cuts as key drivers. While acknowledging downside risks like rising interest rates, other firms like Bank of America Merrill Lynch also see further upside for the market, with fundamentals not yet at peak levels.

title: Warren Buffett Isn’t a Fan of Bonds. But They May Be Good for You. (Published 2018)
summary: Warren Buffett has repeatedly voiced his skepticism about bonds, calling them "a terrible mistake" for long-term investors due to low yields and the potential for losses when interest rates rise. However, the author argues that bonds can still serve as a valuable risk dampener for most investors, even if their recent performance was subdued. Most investors lack Buffett's unique market insights and deep pockets, making bonds a suitable component for diversifying their portfolios.

title: Bank Earnings Boom as Regulators Relax Rules
summary: JPMorgan Chase and Citigroup reported strong first-quarter results in 2018, driven by turbulent markets boosting trading desks and rising interest rates benefiting core lending. The banks also reduced capital cushions, anticipating relaxed regulations from the Trump administration, which could lead to increased share repurchases, dividends, and lending. This signals a potential new era of vigor for the banking industry after years of subdued performance.

title: How I Own My Gold
summary: Axel Merk discusses various ways to own gold, evaluating the pros and cons of physical gold, gold miners, and gold ETFs, including his own VanEck Merk Gold Trust (OUNZ). He delves into the emotional aspect of gold ownership, counterparty risks, and the benefits of diversification in a portfolio. The article emphasizes making informed decisions about gold investments, considering liquidity, storage, and tax implications across different ownership methods.

title: Franklin FTSE Australia ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:FLAU) $FLAU
summary: The Franklin FTSE Australia ETF (FLAU) tracks a market cap-weighted index of large- and mid-cap Australian stocks and was launched in November 2017. Key statistics include $179.63 million in market capitalization, $212.29 million in assets under management, and a net expense ratio of 0.09%.

title: U.S. Bank Profit Fueled by Higher Interest Rates, Lower Taxes
summary: U.S. Bancorp reported a 13% increase in first-quarter earnings, attributed to higher interest rates and a reduced tax levy, with profit reaching $1.68 billion. The company's per-share earnings of 96 cents surpassed analyst expectations. Despite strong interest-related income, fee income was lower than anticipated, causing the stock to fall 2% on Wednesday.

title: iShares 0-5 Year TIPS Bond ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:STIP) $STIP
summary: The iShares 0-5 Year TIPS Bond ETF (STIP) tracks an index of US Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS) with maturities under 5 years, launched in December 2010 and managed by BlackRock. As of March 13, 2026, STIP was trading at $103.38 with a 3.93% dividend yield and $14.42 billion in assets under management. The article provides current price, key statistics, recent news including monthly distributions, and top holdings of the ETF.

title: Punishing Wells Fargo: Just Deserts, or Beating a Dead Horse? (Published 2018)
summary: Wells Fargo is facing a new potential $1 billion penalty for infractions related to mortgages and auto loans, adding to billions in previous fines for its fake accounts scandal and mortgage-backed securities issues. This new penalty follows a Federal Reserve ruling in February that barred the bank from expanding its balance sheet beyond $2 trillion. The article questions whether these punishments are sufficient or if regulators are now "beating a dead horse."

title: SPY Chart, Investor Sentiment Echo November 2016 Stock Market
summary: The article discusses the stock market's resistance at key technical levels and the lingering influence of FOMC rate hikes. It highlights how current investor sentiment, specifically low equity allocations and technical indicators, echoes the pre-November 2016 election period. The author suggests that a resolution to trade war concerns, similar to the removal of election uncertainty in 2016, may be needed to push the S&P 500 above resistance.

title: Warren Buffett isn’t a fan of bonds. But they may be good for you.
summary: Despite Warren Buffett's negative stance on bonds, this article suggests they may still be beneficial for most investors as a tool to reduce volatility and provide courage during stock market downturns. Financial experts explain that while bond returns are currently low and the market is experiencing a "bear market" for bonds, varying duration strategies and alternatives like CDs or floating-rate bonds can still serve important portfolio diversification and stability goals.

title: Which Is Best: REITs or Real Estate Crowdfunding?
summary: This article compares REITs and real estate crowdfunding as two different paths to invest in real estate without the direct burden of property management. It highlights the benefits and drawbacks of each, including liquidity, customization, and accessibility for different types of investors. The article concludes that both options can be smart moves in a rising interest rate environment.

title: A Highly Liquid, High-Yield Bond ETF Option
summary: The article highlights the Xtrackers USD High Yield Corporate Bond ETF (HYLB) as a strong option for investors seeking high-yield debt exposure. It notes HYLB's significant assets under management, low expense ratio, attractive yield, and high liquidity. The fund offers pure high-yield beta exposure and is described as less impacted by interest rate changes, providing a yield cushion for investors.

title: A High-Yield, Alt Strategy for Rising Rate Environment
summary: Tom Lydon discussed the VanEck Vectors BDC Income ETF (BIZD) as a high-yield, alternative strategy for investors seeking income in a rising interest rate environment. Business Development Companies (BDCs) fund small- to mid-sized private companies, often with floating-rate loans, which benefit from increasing interest rates. This makes BDCs a potentially attractive option as traditional lenders face tighter regulations.

title: Nine Proposals in Equities, Debt, Convertibles and Multi-Assets from the Investment & Golf Summit 2018 Organized by Funds Society in Miami
summary: Funds Society's fifth Investment & Golf Summit featured nine asset managers presenting investment proposals across equities, debt, convertibles, and multi-assets. The summit, held in Miami, concentrated on strategies for a volatile environment with a focus on US inflation and Fed rate hikes. Key discussions covered opportunities in Chinese equities, small-caps, dynamic high-yield fixed income, MBS, emerging debt, convertibles, and diversified multi-asset portfolios.

title: HDFC Bank raises FD rates by 10-100 bps for various tenures
summary: HDFC Bank has increased fixed deposit (FD) rates by 10-100 basis points for most tenures above one year, reaching a high of 7% for non-bulk FDs of 1 year 17 days to 5 years. This move, following similar actions by other banks like SBI, aims to attract deposits to address tightening liquidity conditions where credit growth is outpacing deposit growth. The increased cost of funds for banks is expected to impact MCLR-linked loans, making them costlier.

title: Wheat, First Securities - Raymond James - Commentaries
summary: Jeffrey Saut of Raymond James discusses market performance, Dow Theory signals, and inflation concerns. He analyzes Point & Figure charting for the D-J Industrials and reviews strong Q1 2018 corporate earnings and revenue growth, suggesting a transition to an earnings-driven secular bull market.

title: How to Find Relative Value in Inflation-Linked Bonds
summary: This article discusses how to find relative value in inflation-linked bonds, which are securities designed to protect investors from inflation. It covers the market size, how these bonds fit into a portfolio, and the use of inflation swaps and break-even inflation rates as future indicators. The author also provides strategies for relative value analysis and hedging inflation risk, including an example of regression hedging using inflation-linked and nominal bonds.

title: This Week's ETF Launches: BlackRock Hedges One of Its Biggest Bond ETFs Against Inflation
summary: BlackRock has launched a new ETF, the iShares Inflation Hedged Corporate Bond ETF (LQDI), to help investors protect against inflation. This ETF layers inflation swap contracts and other instruments over BlackRock's popular corporate bond fund (LQD) to provide a hedge against rising inflation while still investing in corporate bonds for added yield. It's noted as the first fund to apply inflation hedging techniques to a corporate bond fund.

title: Are You Prepared for Rising Rates?
summary: This article discusses strategies for investors to prepare for rising interest rates, primarily focusing on bond laddering with defined maturity ETFs. It explains how a bond ladder allows for reinvestment of maturing proceeds at potentially higher rates and highlights the benefits of defined maturity ETFs for income generation, diversification, and liquidity. The article also mentions Invesco's BulletShares suite as an option for such investments.

title: A Currency Hedge For Developed Markets
summary: As the U.S. dollar strengthens, investors should consider currency hedging for international equities and ETFs. The iShares Currency Hedged MSCI EAFE ETF (HEFA) offers a diversified portfolio of developed market stocks, excluding the U.S., Canada, and emerging markets, while mitigating currency risk. This strategy can reduce volatility for international investments, especially when central banks outside the U.S. are not normalizing monetary policies in sync with the Federal Reserve.

title: Campbell Soup CEO out, steel tariffs to bite soon
summary: Denise Morrison, CEO of Campbell Soup since 2011, is retiring and will be replaced by interim CEO Keith McLoughlin. The company is undergoing a strategic review as it faces declining sales, rising costs, and the impact of steel and aluminum tariffs. Campbell's also reported a third-quarter loss and lowered its full-year earnings projections.

title: Short-Term Bond ETFs Play a Role in Any Environment
summary: Short-term bond ETFs offer benefits beyond mitigating rising interest rate risks, playing an important role in various interest-rate and economic environments. They can provide prompt reinvestment at higher rates during rising interest rate periods and offer higher income alternatives than cash investments in slow-growth environments. Actively managed short-duration ETFs like the Natixis Loomis Sayles Short Duration Income ETF (NYSEArca: LSST) can adapt to changing market conditions and potentially outperform an index.

title: Spiking AutoZone shares roll completely over and tank on cost concerns raised on earnings call
summary: AutoZone shares dropped significantly after concerns about rising costs and labor inflation were raised during its quarterly earnings call. CEO William Rhodes indicated that selling, general and administrative expenses are expected to increase in fiscal year 2019 due to wage raises. This news erased earlier gains caused by stronger-than-expected earnings for the fiscal third quarter.

title: Yields Look Overextended and Ready for Mean Reversion
summary: Frank Holmes argues that the 10-year Treasury yield is overdue for a mean reversion, suggesting a potential decline from its current overextended levels. The article highlights the historical outperformance and lower volatility of municipal bonds compared to Treasuries during rate hike cycles, and notes that recent tax reforms may make munis even more attractive due to capped SALT deductions. Investors are encouraged to consider short-term muni bond funds for tax-free income and capital preservation.

title: Cramer Remix: Don’t let this buying opportunity pass again
summary: Jim Cramer highlighted FMC Corp. as a strong buying opportunity due to its recent dip, despite strong fundamentals in both the agricultural and lithium sectors. He also discussed the market's reaction to Netflix surpassing Disney in market cap, dismissed inflation worries, and interviewed the CEOs of Indigo Agriculture and Intuit about their companies' innovative approaches.
